experiment: P3o-M resolution-aware sparse-delay-event ordinal MFT-count screen
research_question: On fresh compound I/Q identities, does explicitly selecting sparse, reference-deconvolved local delay events improve MFT target-count ordinal estimation beyond an equal-token fixed-delay-bin control?

prior_boundary.P3c: exact MFT component plus correct reference is physically sufficient; raw compound threshold counting saturates
prior_boundary.P3d: a dense inverse-delay CNN ordinal head failed in ultra-close and did not satisfy all-regime gates; its identities and hyperparameters are frozen

roles.constant_baseline: median count fitted on fit identities only
roles.development: all 33 identities per combination; read exactly once after method freeze

front_end.candidate_C1: strict local maxima, rank by contrast, retain up to 16, then restore temporal order and zero-pad
front_end.equal_information_control_C0: partition the same delay window into 16 fixed bins and retain the maximum-contrast point per bin

models.C0_fixed_bin: identical four-channel, 16-token ordinal CNN; fixed-bin tokenization
models.C1_sparse_peak: identical four-channel, 16-token ordinal CNN; sparse local-peak tokenization
models.ordinal_output: seven cumulative logits decoded to count 1 through 8

stop_rule: If any promotion gate fails, stop P3o-M. Do not tune token count, peak rule, network width, loss, training schedule, or attach the expert on seeds 1570M/1580M. Do not generate confirmation identities.
next_if_pass: Freeze code/checkpoints/normalizer and evaluate a predicted-label-gated MFT-only attachment on the two untouched confirmation identities; it must preserve classification logits and improve worst-combination predicted-gate risk before any all-12 claim.
